subject: Banking
title: Signature Bank and the Crypto Connection
description: A fast breakdown of Signature Bank and the Crypto Connection for builders.

hook.text: Signature Bank failed in March 2023, two days after SVB. It had become the banking partner for crypto firms.

buildup.text: Signature embraced crypto deposits when other banks wouldn't. Its Signet platform let crypto companies move money 24/7.

discovery.text: When crypto markets crashed and FTX collapsed, Signature lost billions in deposits.

twist.text: Regulators seized Signature before depositors could run.

climax.text: Signature showed that new industries bring new risks. Serving crypto clients made a bank vulnerable to crypto crises.

punchline.text: Embraced crypto. Crypto crashed. The bank failed two days after SVB.

quiz.question: What made Signature Bank uniquely vulnerable?
options: Heavy dependence on cryptocurrency industry deposits

details.summary: Signature Bank was closed by regulators in March 2023 after a rapid deposit outflow driven by its heavy exposure to cryptocurrency clients. Its failure, alongside Silicon Valley Bank, raised questions about the banking system's resilience to digital panics.
details.whyItMatters: Signature Bank's failure demonstrated that concentration in a single volatile industry can be fatal. Its crypto-heavy deposit base proved to be a liability when the crypto market collapsed.
takeaways: Signature Bank had roughly 20 percent of deposits from crypto firms
The bank was seized two days after Silicon Valley Bank's collapse
Signature was the third-largest bank failure in US history at $110 billion

faq.question: Was Signature Bank's failure caused by cryptocurrency?
faq.answer: Crypto exposure contributed but was not the sole cause. The crypto winter reduced deposits, and SVB's collapse triggered a broader panic among uninsured depositors. Signature's concentrated client base made it especially vulnerable to contagion fear.

faq.question: What happened to Signature Bank's depositors?
faq.answer: Regulators guaranteed all deposits, including those above the $250,000 FDIC limit, to prevent further contagion. Flagstar Bank acquired most of Signature's deposits and certain loan portfolios in an FDIC-managed resolution.
